title: Bar chart: minutes by genre
prompt: Driftlight's content team wants to see which genres people watch most. Build horizontal bars of total minutes watched per genre, with the longest bar at the top.
hints: Horizontal bars put the dimension on Rows and the measure on Columns.
Open the Genre pill's menu and sort it by the field Minutes Watched, descending.
debrief: A discrete dimension on Rows gives one header per member, and a measure on Columns gives a continuous axis, so Automatic draws bars. Sorting by a measure is a computed sort: it keeps up when the data changes, unlike a manual order.

title: Line chart: minutes per month
prompt: Show how total minutes watched moved month by month across 2024 and 2025 as one continuous line.
hints: Start is a date. Dropped on a shelf it starts as YEAR(Start), a discrete date part.
In the pill's menu, pick Month under the date values, not the date parts.
debrief: A date value (here, the month truncation) is continuous: it draws a green pill and a time axis, and Automatic picks a line. MONTH as a date part would instead be discrete and put January 2024 and January 2025 into the same header.

title: Line chart: one line per title type
prompt: Split the monthly line of total minutes watched into one coloured line for each title type.
hints: A dimension on Color splits the marks and gives each member its own colour.
debrief: A discrete field on Color adds a level of detail to the view: SUM(Minutes Watched) is now computed per month and per type, and each type gets a colour from a categorical palette.

title: Date parts: quarters inside years
prompt: Compare the four quarters of each year: build bars of total minutes watched with a header per year and, inside it, one bar per quarter.
hints: You need Start twice on Columns.
Keep the first one as YEAR and change the second one to the QUARTER date part.
With a date and a measure, Automatic draws a line: choose Bar on the Marks card.
debrief: Date parts are discrete, so each one draws headers (blue pills) and the view splits into panes. Q1 means the first quarter of the year in its header, not one continuous stretch of time.

title: Stacked bar: devices in each region
prompt: Show total minutes watched per region as vertical bars, with each bar split into the devices people watched on.
hints: Build the region bars first, then drop the dimension that should split each bar on Color.
debrief: A dimension on Color of a bar chart stacks the bars: each segment is SUM(Minutes Watched) for one region and device, and the whole bar is the region's total.

title: Crosstab: minutes by region and year
prompt: Finance wants the exact numbers, not bars: a text table with a row per region, a column per year and total minutes watched in each cell.
hints: Only discrete pills go on Columns and Rows here, so there is no axis.
Put the measure on Label (Tableau calls it Text in a text table).
debrief: With discrete pills on both shelves there are only headers, so Automatic picks the text mark and the measure is written into each cell. This is a crosstab, also called a text table.

title: Highlight table: sessions by weekday and device
prompt: Show the number of sessions for each device and weekday as a table whose cells are shaded by the count, with the count written in each cell.
hints: Weekday is a date part of Start.
A highlight table is a crosstab with the Square mark and the measure on Color as well as on Label.
debrief: A continuous measure on Color shades each cell on a sequential scale, which turns a crosstab into a highlight table. The Square mark fills the cells.

title: Scatterplot: runtime against catalogue size
prompt: Using the Titles data source, plot one mark per sub-genre: average runtime across, number of titles up, coloured by genre.
hints: Runtime is summed by default. Change its aggregation to Average.
With two measures there is only one mark until a dimension on Detail splits it.
debrief: Two continuous measures make a scatterplot. On their own they aggregate to a single mark for the whole data source; Sub-Genre on Detail sets the level of detail to one mark per sub-genre without adding headers.

title: Symbol map: subscribers per city
prompt: Using the Subscribers data source, draw a world map with one circle per city, sized by the number of subscribers.
hints: Longitude goes on Columns and Latitude on Rows: use the generated ones, which come from the geographic role.
City on Detail gives one mark per city; the count goes on Size.
debrief: Fields with a geographic role give Tableau generated latitude and longitude. Each mark sits at the place named by the finest geographic field in the view, and a measure on Size scales the circles.

title: Filled map: subscribers per country
prompt: Using the Subscribers data source, shade each country by its number of subscribers.
hints: Start like a symbol map with Country on Detail, then change the mark type to Map and colour by the count.
debrief: The Map mark fills each country's shape. A continuous measure on Color shades the shapes on a sequential scale: this is a filled map (choropleth).

title: Density map: where subscribers live
prompt: Using the Subscribers data source, plot every subscriber at their own latitude and longitude, drawn with the Density mark so clusters stand out.
hints: Here use the Latitude and Longitude fields from the data, not the generated ones.
Subscriber ID on Detail gives one mark per subscriber.
debrief: A density map needs many overlapping marks, so the level of detail is one mark per subscriber. The Density mark blends overlapping marks into hot spots.

title: Aggregation: average session length by plan
prompt: Product wants to know how long a typical session lasts on each plan. Show the average minutes watched per session for each plan as horizontal bars.
hints: Minutes Watched lands as SUM(Minutes Watched). Change the aggregation in its pill menu.
debrief: A measure gets its default aggregation (here SUM) when it is dropped on a shelf. The question asks about a typical session, so the aggregation has to change to AVG: same field, different question.

title: Count distinct: active subscribers by region
prompt: Using the Sessions data source, show how many different subscribers watched something in each region, as horizontal bars.
hints: Subscriber ID is a dimension. On Columns it would give one header per subscriber.
Its pill menu can turn it into a measure: Count (Distinct).
debrief: A dimension can be aggregated into a measure. COUNTD counts each subscriber once per region, however many sessions they had; a plain count of sessions would be much larger.

title: Dimension filter: genres on TV
prompt: Show total minutes watched per genre as horizontal bars, counting only sessions watched on a TV.
hints: Drag Device to the Filters shelf and keep only TV.
debrief: A dimension filter removes rows before anything is aggregated, so every bar now sums TV sessions only. Device doesn't have to be in the view to filter by it.

title: Date filter: 2025 only
prompt: Show total minutes watched month by month as a continuous line, for 2025 only.
hints: Drag Start to Filters. Either keep the year 2025, or set a range of dates covering the whole year.
debrief: A date filter can keep date parts (the year 2025) or a range of dates (1 January to 31 December 2025). Both give the same view here; relative dates are a third option in Tableau.

title: Combined axis: two kinds of minutes
prompt: Show average minutes watched and average runtime per session month by month, as two lines on one shared axis.
hints: Set Runtime's default aggregation to Average, or change it on the card afterwards.
Open Runtime in the Data pane and choose Drop on the Rows axis: the two measures then share the axis.
debrief: Dropping a measure on an existing axis makes a combined (blended) axis: Measure Values on the shelf, the measures on the Measure Values card and Measure Names on Color. It suits measures in the same units, as here, where both are minutes.

title: Dual axis: bars and a line
prompt: Show minutes watched per month as bars and the number of sessions per month as a line, each on its own axis.
hints: Open the second measure's pill menu and choose Dual Axis.
With two measures on a shelf the Marks card has a tab for each: set the minutes tab to Bar.
debrief: A dual axis layers two measures in one pane, each with its own axis and its own Marks card, so one can be bars and the other a line. It suits measures with different units or scales, such as minutes and sessions.

title: Above or below average
prompt: Draw minutes watched per genre as bars, with one reference line at the average of the bars across the whole table.
hints: Open the Analytics pane and add an Average Line.
Choose Table as the scope: one line for the whole view.
debrief: A reference line's scope decides how many lines you get: Table draws one, Pane one per pane, Cell one per cell. Its value is a constant or a computation over the marks, such as the average.

title: Each genre's share
prompt: Show each genre's share of all minutes watched as bars that add up to 100%.
hints: Open the SUM(Minutes Watched) pill's menu and choose Quick Table Calculation.
debrief: Percent of total is a quick table calculation: it divides each mark by the total of the marks it computes over. The pill gets a delta (△) to show a table calculation is applied.

title: The year building up
prompt: Show minutes watched as a continuous line by month, where each point is the total so far.
hints: A total so far is a running total, one of the quick table calculations on the measure's pill.
debrief: A running total adds each mark to all the marks before it along the Compute Using direction. Quick table calculations compute over the marks in the view, not over the rows.

title: How long are sessions?
prompt: Count sessions in 10-minute ranges of minutes watched: a histogram.
hints: Open Minutes Watched in the Data pane and choose Create > Bins, with a size of 10.
Put the bin field on Columns and Minutes Watched on Rows, then change its aggregation to Count.
debrief: Bins cut a measure into equal ranges and create a new dimension; the lower limit of each bin is inclusive. A histogram counts the marks in each bin, which is why the measure aggregates as CNT.

title: Hours, not minutes
prompt: Create a calculated field Hours Watched (minutes divided by 60) and show its total per device as bars.
hints: In the Data pane, create a calculated field named Hours Watched.
The formula divides [Minutes Watched] by 60. It's a row-level number, so Tableau treats it as a measure and sums it.
debrief: A row-level calculation is computed for every row and then aggregated in the view, so SUM(Hours Watched) is the total minutes divided by 60. A number calc becomes a measure in the Data pane.

title: Crosstab with grand totals
prompt: Show minutes watched in a crosstab of region by year, with a grand total for every region and every year.
hints: Totals are in the Totals menu (Analysis > Totals), or drag Totals from the Analytics pane.
You need both: row grand totals (a column at the right) and column grand totals (a row at the bottom).
debrief: Row grand totals add a Grand Total column; column grand totals add a Grand Total row. Totals need at least one header, and Total All Using chooses how they aggregate.

title: One Cologne
prompt: Count German subscribers by city, with Cologne and Köln combined into one bar and Munich and München into another.
hints: Open City in the Data pane and choose Create > Group, or select two bars and click Group.
Keep the default name City (group), put it on Rows in place of City, and make two groups: Cologne with Köln, Munich with München.
debrief: A group combines members of a field into bigger members, the classic fix for spelling variants. The other cities stay as they are unless you include Other.

title: Where the top 10 titles sit
prompt: Show minutes watched per genre as bars, coloured by whether the minutes come from the top 10 titles by minutes or not.
hints: Open Title in the Data pane and choose Create > Set; use the Top tab: top 10 by SUM(Minutes Watched).
Put the set on Color: it shows In and Out.
debrief: A set made on the Top tab is dynamic: when viewing changes, so do its members. On Color it splits each bar into In and Out of the set.
